{{search|criminals who hunt and sell Pokémon|the type of Trainer in the [[Generation III]] [[side series]] games|Hunter (Trainer class)}} ---- [[File:Masked Marauder Dark Ball.png|thumb|250px|The Iron-Masked Marauder in ''[[M04|Celebi: The Voice of the Forest]]'']] A '''Pokémon hunter''', also known as a '''Pokémon poacher''' (Japanese: '''ポケモンハンター''' ''Pokémon hunter''), is typically a [[Human|person]] who captures [[wild Pokémon]], sometimes many of the same [[Pokémon (species)|species]] at a time, to sell for profit. They often use exceptionally powerful Pokémon. Some Pokémon hunters also attempt to steal Pokémon from their {{pkmn|Trainer}}s. For a list of Pokémon hunters, see [[:Category:Pokémon hunters]]. ==In the games== In the {{pkmn|games}}, people who steal Pokémon are often referred to as '''Pokémon thieves'''. Relatedly, in the [[core series]], if the player attempts to [[Caught Pokémon|catch]] a Pokémon belonging to another {{pkmn|Trainer}}, a message will appear, typically stating the phrase "Don't be a thief". This phrase is referenced by [[Looker]] in {{game|Platinum}}. This is also [[List of cross-canon references|referenced in the animated series]] in the {{aniseries|JN}} episode ''[[JN059|When a House is Not a Home!]]'', where [[Goh]]'s [[Rotom Phone]] says the phrase when he attempts to catch a {{TP|Goh|Grookey}} that's already owned by [[Rocket Prize Master|someone else]]. In the [[side series]], [[Team Snagem]] is a gang of Pokémon thieves that steal Pokémon from their Trainers using the [[Snag Machine]]. [[Lorelei]] also refers to '''poachers''' in {{game|FireRed and LeafGreen|s}}. '''Hunters''' are occasionally referenced in [[Pokédex entry|Pokédex entries]], although this is typically in reference to people hunting [[wild Pokémon]] in order [[Pokémon predation#Humans eating Pokémon|to eat them]], rather than poaching Pokémon for profit. However, exceptions apply, such as {{p|Persian}} being hunted for the valuable jewel embedded in its forehead. ==In animation== [[File:J anime.png|thumb|250px|[[J|Pokémon Hunter J]] in {{aniseries|DP}}]] ===''Pokémon the Series''=== [[Team Rocket]] was the first major organization shown in the {{pkmn|animated series}} to steal Pokémon for profit. The first major hunter to appear in a movie, the [[Iron-Masked Marauder]], was also a member of Team Rocket. As the main antagonist of ''[[M04|Celebi: The Voice of the Forest]]'', he planned to use a sinister [[Poké Ball]], called the [[Dark Ball]], to [[Caught Pokémon|capture]] and control {{OBP|Celebi|M04}}. [[J|Pokémon Hunter J]] was the first recurring Pokémon hunter in the series. She traveled through the [[Sinnoh]] [[region]] with her {{TP|J|henchmen}}, stealing Pokémon on behalf of her clients, who often gave large sums of money in exchange. Like the Iron-Masked Marauder, she often used underhanded tactics and devious {{DL|J|gadgets}} to achieve her goals. Pokémon hunters tend to be far more dangerous than other villains in the series, as they typically have no qualms about having their Pokémon attack humans directly or using [[Weaponry in the Pokémon world|guns and other weapons]] to attack their target. This is most often shown by Hunter J, who in ''[[DP072|Pokémon Ranger and the Kidnapped Riolu! Part 2]]'' seemed to try to [[Death in the Pokémon world|kill]] Ash repeatedly. Similarly, the Pokémon hunter [[Rico]] had his Pokémon attack [[Jessie]] and [[James]] in ''[[AG006|A Poached Ego!]]''. ====Notable hunters==== * [[Dirk]] * [[Iron-Masked Marauder]] * [[J|Hunter J]] * [[Rico]] * [[Dolan]] ===''The Power of Us''=== In ''[[M21|The Power of Us]]'', a movie which takes place in [[I Choose You!
